items.title: Charlie Cordilla Interview, 1952-05-17
items.q: You never did play with Tony, what's his name? Perranti. Tony Perranti, no. No, I've never played with Tony.

ctx.x: My name is Charlie Joseph Cadilla. I was born in Baton Rouge, May the 25th, 1899. Joe, is your middle name? Joseph. Charles Joseph. And when did you move to New Orleans? Oh, when I was about six years old. How many brothers and sisters did you have? Five boys and four girls. And they're all living still? All but one. Is that so? Were you the oldest or the youngest? No, I'm the youngest. The youngest? That's a pretty good record. How many kids you got of your own? None. Married how long? It'll be 27 years,…

the drums do. Now let's go back to Union's Rhythm King session. Yeah. Because those are historical records. Rap is on quite a number of them. Yeah. And then he suddenly disappears. And that was the result of that deal with Santo. That's right. That one particular record, which was one side was She's Crying For Me Blues. It was Santo's number. And I'll never forget that morning.
